title: Machine learning identified predictors of patient-reported stroke rehabilitation outcomes
summary: In retrospective data from 124 people with chronic stroke, machine-learning models predicted post-intervention change in four patient-reported activity and participation outcomes. Baseline outcome scores were among the strongest predictors; best model accuracies ranged from 0.72 to 0.96 with 18 features and 0.72 to 0.84 with reduced feature sets. This small-sample prediction study does not show which individuals causally benefit from rehabilitation or generalize beyond its setting.
ai_technology: Logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, SVM and random forest
organization: National Taiwan University; National Taipei University of Nursing and Health Sciences

evidence.tested: The study used an 80/20 split, stratified ten-fold tuning and a held-out test set. It reused retrospective data from earlier studies and has limited single-context generalizability.
evidence.unknown: No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.
evidence.ai_role: Classification models predicted changes in four patient-reported rehabilitation outcomes and identified outcome-specific predictors.
